headline: Southborough set its FY27 tax rate while town boards began weighing a potential FY28 tax override alongside $40 million Neary School renovation estimates.
synopsis: In November 2026, the Select Board set Southborough's fiscal year 2027 single property tax rate at $14.54 per thousand, resulting in an estimated 5 percent increase on the average single-family tax bill. At the same time, town officials began preparing for an FY28 operating budget deficit of $1.4 million, reviewing dual departmental scenarios that either require a Proposition 2 1/2 override or deep cuts to municipal, police, fire, and school staffing. School and building officials learned that modernizing Neary Elementary School will cost between $33 million and $40 million, confirming that an earlier $15 million target is unfeasible. The Planning Board continued detailed hearings on traffic, stormwater, and landscaping waivers for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco project on Coslin Drive. Meanwhile, the town secured a $632,000 state grant for Fayville Memorial Park improvements, and the Select Board voted to sponsor a zoning amendment expanding 55-plus housing opportunities.

top_items.title: Town Boards Weigh FY28 Budget Deficit and Override Scenarios
top_items.why: Town departments presented level-service and level-funded budgets to address a projected $1.4 million operating deficit. Without a Proposition 2 1/2 override, officials warned of severe cuts to municipal staffing, public safety, and public schools.
top_items.body: The Select Board and Southborough School Committee began reviewing fiscal year 2028 operating budget requests under two mandated frameworks: a level-service Budget A and a level-funded Budget B. Maintaining level services would create an estimated $1.4 million municipal shortfall requiring an operating tax override. Under a level-funded Budget B, departments outlined significant reductions. The police department warned of losing an officer, a dispatcher, and a cruiser; the fire department cited dropping shift staffing from five to three or four, halting second-ambulance operations; and public school administrators indicated that closing a $1.4 million gap would require eliminating approximately 15 full-time staff positions.

top_items.title: Select Board Adopts FY27 Property Tax Rate of $14.54
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to maintain a single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand for fiscal year 2027. The rate leads to an estimated 5.01 percent increase on the average single-family tax bill.
top_items.body: Following the annual tax classification hearing, the Select Board voted 4-1 to maintain a unified property tax rate rather than shifting taxes onto commercial properties. Total town valuation reached $4.072 billion, with the average single-family home value climbing 3.7 percent to $1,027,800. The board also voted 5-0 against adopting residential or small commercial exemptions. The decision translates to an estimated average tax increase of 5.01 percent for residential homeowners.

top_items.title: Neary School Renovation Projected at $33 Million to $40 Million
top_items.why: Architects reported that fully modernizing Neary Elementary School will cost roughly $32.9 million to $39.8 million. The estimates confirm that an earlier $15 million budget concept is unfeasible.
top_items.body: Architects presented detailed cost estimates to the Elementary School Building Committee, demonstrating that meeting basic mechanical, electrical, and building codes at Neary Elementary School will require approximately $32.9 million. Adding educational program enhancements, infilling wide hallways for breakout spaces, and building a full-sized gymnasium in the courtyard under Option 3 would push total costs to $39.8 million. Officials discussed how to present these realistic figures to residents and weighed whether to fund the work locally or submit a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority in January 2027.

top_items.title: Planning Board Evaluates Costco Warehouse Site Plan and Waivers
top_items.why: The Planning Board reviewed traffic, lighting, landscaping, and stormwater waiver requests for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco on Coslin Drive. Deliberations were continued to December 14 ahead of a December 18 decision deadline.
top_items.body: Costco's proposed retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive underwent continued review across two November Planning Board sessions. Discussions focused on regional traffic modeling, Route 9 intersection mitigation, 36.6-foot light poles previously granted variances by the Zoning Board of Appeals, and extensive native plantings. Costco also sought waivers regarding stormwater infiltration standards and rock mulch. With public safety, traffic, and peer engineering reviews continuing, the board continued the hearing to December 14, 2026, and extended its decision deadline to December 18.

top_items.title: Capital Committee Confronts $1 Million Gap for FY28
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed departmental requests totaling $2.2 million against a $1.2 million tax levy target. Requests include smart water meters, DPW trucks, police tech bundles, and school building repairs.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated capital requests exceeding available funding allocations. The Department of Public Works outlined major multi-year needs, including an estimated $1.82 million smart water meter overhaul, a $700,000 rehabilitation of the Tara Road water tank, and $275,000 highway plow trucks. The police department requested a 60-month lease bundle for body cameras and Tasers alongside cruiser replacements, while the K-8 public schools submitted $710,000 in requests for sink replacements, stair repairs, and perimeter fencing. The committee asked departments for phased options and planned to rank and vote on priorities on November 30.

top_items.title: Select Board Sponsors Zoning Amendment to Expand Senior Housing
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to sponsor a Town Meeting zoning amendment lifting the town's 7 percent cap on 55-plus housing. The proposal allows up to eight units per acre on parcels of at least two acres.
top_items.body: The Affordable Housing Trust presented a zoning amendment designed to expand age-restricted senior housing options in town. The proposal eliminates the townwide 7 percent cap on 55-plus housing, sets a two-acre minimum lot size, requires 10 percent open space preservation, allows up to eight units per acre, and mandates a 12.5 percent affordable housing requirement. The Select Board unanimously referred the article to the Planning Board and agreed to sponsor it for the upcoming Town Meeting warrant.

top_items.title: Town Secures $632,000 State Grant for Fayville Park Upgrades
top_items.why: Southborough was awarded a state grant of up to $632,000 from the Land and Water Conservation Fund to cover half of the Fayville Park project costs. The town plans to seek matching Community Preservation Act funds at Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The Recreation Commission and Select Board received confirmation of a Land and Water Conservation Fund grant of up to $632,000, funding half of the planned revitalization of Fayville Memorial Park. The proposed improvements feature a children's splash pad, dog park, walking trail, and accessibility upgrades. Project leaders are coordinating with police and public works officials on roadside parking designs along Central Street and will seek matching funds from the Community Preservation Act at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.
